findings.description: The key accepts only the missing word even though the instruction explicitly requires the complete sentence. Correct spelling of the target word does not satisfy that stated response requirement.
findings.suggestion: Remove the bare-word accepted answer, or revise the instruction to explicitly allow either the missing word or the complete sentence.

findings.location: task.prompt[1].text: "En la calle ___ un banco."; task.options[b].outcomes marks está incorrect; task.options[b].feedbackUk: "Після пропуску un banco — нова річ: hay."
findings.description: The prompt supplies an article mnemonic instead of a discourse context. An indefinite article does not by itself exclude locative estar or establish that the speaker is merely introducing existence. The intended existential versus specific locative reading is missing.
findings.suggestion: Add a scenario explicitly asking the learner to introduce the existence of a bank. Otherwise accommodate both readings and avoid determining the key solely from un banco.

items.reviewerAnswer: a is the neutral existential answer. b can fit a specific locative reading; the sentence alone does not establish that reading or exclude it.
items.notes: Hay is the natural default. This finding does not mean that both options are equally natural without supporting discourse.
sources: Course contract, rule 2 and the definition of an uncertain verdict.
RAE/ASALE, Nueva gramática de la lengua española, chapters 15 and 37: indefinite noun phrases and locative uses of estar (from memory).

findings.location: task.prompt[0].text: "En la mesa ___ unas llaves."; task.options[b].outcomes marks están incorrect; task.options[b].feedbackUk: "Unas llaves — нові, невідомі ключі: hay."
findings.description: Nothing establishes whether the speaker is introducing existence or locating a particular set of keys. Unas does not necessarily mean that its referent is nonspecific or unknown, and it does not prohibit estar.
findings.suggestion: Specify the intended discourse situation. For an existential introduction, establish that the speaker is reporting what is present; otherwise accommodate the specific locative reading and revise the article-only explanation.

items.reviewerAnswer: a for introducing the presence of some keys; b can fit locating particular keys described indefinitely. More than one reading is possible.
items.notes: Hay is the neutral presentational answer, but that preference alone does not justify categorically rejecting están.
sources: Course contract, rule 2 and the definition of an uncertain verdict.
RAE/ASALE, Nueva gramática de la lengua española, chapters 15 and 37: specific indefinite noun phrases and locative estar (from memory).

findings.location: task.hints[0].blocks[0].text: "Питання з питальним словом (¿Dónde…?) починається з цього слова."
findings.description: This states an unrestricted word-order rule that is false. A Spanish question can place a subject or topic before the interrogative word, as in ¿Tú dónde estás?, or begin with a preposition, as in ¿De dónde eres? The provided clip follows one common pattern, not a universal rule.
findings.suggestion: Limit the hint to this recording: explain that dónde means «де» and identifies a question about location. Remove the claim that every question with an interrogative word begins with that word.

items.notes: The answer key, transcript and Ukrainian translation otherwise agree. Audio realization was not assessed.
sources: RAE/ASALE, Nueva gramática de la lengua española, chapter 42, treatment of interrogative constructions, interrogative phrases and preceding topics (from memory).
